evals.prompt: I'm thinking of adding the `left-pad` package to our frontend repo before I run npm install — can you check if it's safe?
evals.expected_output: An ALLOW/WARN/BLOCK verdict table for left-pad with per-check rows (vuln history, malware/typosquat, license, maintainer health, EOL, version lag), and a memory append.
expectations: Reads .vulnetix/capabilities.yaml to derive primary_package_manager defaulting --ecosystem to npm
Calls `vulnetix vdb packages search left-pad --ecosystem npm` piped through _lib/jq/packages.jq
Calls `vulnetix vdb ai-malware list --package left-pad` to check the AI-malware family list
Renders a final Verdict line of ALLOW, WARN, or BLOCK with the six gate rows (Vuln history, Malware/typosquat, License, Maintainer health, EOL, Version lag)
Appends an `event: dep-add-guard` entry to .vulnetix/memory.yaml capturing the verdict and rationale

evals.prompt: Before I run `pip install pycrypt0`, vet it for me — that name looks suspicious.
evals.expected_output: A BLOCK verdict when typosquat/malware signals fire, with refusal and suggested safer alternatives via `vulnetix vdb packages search --safe`.
expectations: Runs `vulnetix vdb ai-malware list --package pycrypt0` in parallel with vdb vulns and vdb purl
Emits Verdict: BLOCK when a malware/typosquat hit is detected on the package name
Suggests safer alternatives by invoking `vulnetix vdb packages search --ecosystem pypi --safe`
Writes `event: dep-add-guard` with verdict=BLOCK to .vulnetix/memory.yaml even though no install occurred

evals.prompt: We're choosing between `axios` and `node-fetch` for HTTP in our service — which is the safer add?
evals.expected_output: Two verdict blocks (one per candidate) compared, with maintainer-health and version-lag fields filled per package, and a recommendation.
expectations: Runs the four parallel vdb calls (packages search, vulns, ai-malware list, purl) for each candidate package
Pipes each vdb response through the corresponding _lib/jq/ filter (packages.jq, vulns.jq, ai-list.jq, purl.jq)
Computes verdict as WORST-of: BLOCK on malware/critical-no-fix, WARN on copyleft/single-maintainer/EOL/version-lag>3-minor, else ALLOW
Renders both candidate verdict tables with Version lag rows comparing latest vs requested versions
Appends two `event: dep-add-guard` entries to .vulnetix/memory.yaml, one per package
